label: COMMUNICATION

cover.headline: Money, chores, in-laws: *5 calmer openers*
cover.sub: For the topics that tend to go sideways.

points.heading: Ask for a time first
points.body: Touchy topics go better by appointment than by ambush.
points.panel: “Can we find twenty minutes this weekend to talk about the budget?”

points.heading: Start with the shared goal
points.body: Open with what you both want. It puts you on the same side of the table.
points.panel: “I want us both to feel less stressed about money.”

points.heading: Describe, don’t diagnose
points.body: Say what happened, not what it says about him.
points.panel: “I’ve ended up doing the dishes most nights lately.”

points.heading: Ask for his read
points.body: You have half the picture. Ask for the other half before you offer a solution.
points.panel: “How does it look from your side?”

points.heading: Propose a trial, not a ruling
points.body: A two-week experiment is easier to agree to than a permanent rule.
points.panel: “Could we try it this way for two weeks and see?”

close.save: Save this for the next touchy topic.

caption:
Most couples have a few topics that seem to arrive with the fuse already lit. Money, chores, and family are common ones.

You can’t make them easy, but you can make the opening calmer, and the opening sets the tone for the rest. Here are five ways in.
